product_from_film: Lexius adds incident detection, phone alerts, footage search and case tracking to existing security cameras.
explains_well: The same shop scene appears first without and then with tracking overlays, followed by a phone alert and review clip.
unclear: The film jumps from detection to broader case and return-person claims without showing how a person reviews or corrects an alert.
scenario: A shoplifting-themed example introduces detection, then footage search, case building, fall alerts and multi-store return tracking.
product_clear_basis: Tracking overlays lead to a phone notification and review clip at 11s; existing-camera use is named at 14s.

sound.detail: The draft contains only the opening question about shoplifting being acceptable. It supports that opening theme, not narration for later features. No music, effects, voice delivery or synchronization was heard or verified.
sound.visual_relation: V01 only; the later explanation comes from visible text and UI.
sound.evidence: 315-speech.json single draft segment at 3.3s; chronological visual samples.

categories.finding: Missed event → detection and phone alert → existing-camera use → search/cases/other alerts → benefits.
The opening uses a concrete store-camera scene before the problem title.
Retail operators with existing cameras are clearly targeted by store scenes and explicit compatibility wording.
Tracking boxes and pose lines change with the person; clip tiles and case/map cards accumulate across sampled states. Exact animation mechanics are unverified.
The same store scene bridges untreated footage, detection overlay and phone review, giving the initial sequence continuity.
Low-resolution camera footage contrasts with white UI and purple/pink brand text; detection uses green/red.
Large feature labels are clear. Small alert labels and case details receive less reading time.
One ASR question supports the opening theme; later script and all delivery are unknown.
categories.reason: Single draft segment, no validated listening.

categories.finding: Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Surveillance-style clips, phone mockups, camera footage, map graphics and title cards are used. Their production sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Most features are named on screen and the initial alert chain can be understood visually.
Detection boxes direct attention to an event; the phone review and enlarged clip focus the next step.
The first 18s establish detection and compatibility, then several features arrive in about 27s.
A phone review clip answers how an event reaches someone, but human review and resolution do not appear.
Problem/solution titles suggest urgency and reassurance. The absolute Shoplifting is over claim exceeds what the shown alert alone establishes.
categories.reason: Film wording and visual evidence, not measured audience response.

categories.finding: Existing store cameras remain the recurring source across alerts, search and cases.
Detection accuracy, identity matching, compatibility and prevention are unverified claims. People shown are not independently established as offenders; that is the film’s labeling.
The camera-to-phone review sequence is a concrete mechanism within a broad security promise.
Add the reviewer decision after the alert.
